### Season outlook as written in the guide (p. 330)

The Indiana Hoosiers won 10 of their 16 victories by 14+ points. One of the six games came against Old Dominion, who was badly outgained in the regular- season opener, but lost 27-14 in what turned out to be a sign of things to come. Ricky Rahne’s program put it all together and improved by five wins to finish 10-3. What is amazing, though, is that ODU’s three losses were by 13, 24, and 36 points, as they were -5 in turnovers against Marshall and got pummeled by James Madison. Otherwise, 10 wins was one fewer than the previous two seasons combined. These whiplash sorts of seasons are very possible at the G6 level nowadays thanks to the portal, as some teams get completely wrecked and others stay intact enough to take advantage. This season, ODU is one of those teams with very heavy losses, including QB Colton Joseph to Wisconsin after rushing for more than 1,000 yards and throwing for over 2,600 more. He’s hardly the only loss, as OC Kevin Decker now holds the same role at Memphis, but Rahne has a favorable schedule to work with. Over 7.5 The schedule is kind to Rahne this season, as James Madison and Marshall go to Norfolk and the non-conference road game at UConn, albeit randomly timed, is very winnable, along with hapless Georgia State, newcomer Louisiana Tech, and a Coastal Carolina team in a transitional phase. Drawing Southern Miss and LA Tech from the West Division isn’t bad at all and the East Carolina game can be had at home. I have them favored in nine games, with +1.5 and +0.5 in two other games, and a projection of 7.51 wins.

## 26. Open Questions / Risks

The guide's *Three Burning Questions for the 2026 Season* *(p. 331)*, with the answers as written:

### Can Cook keep the offense cooking?

Kody Cook is the new OC after serving as the wide receivers coach last season. He’s also the new QB coach with some shifting across the staff. The Monarchs relied very heavily on their top three receivers last season, as only three guys had 11+ catches and they had 762, 719, and 667 yards while nobody else had more than 200. All three of those guys are gone, so Cook’s old position group needs to be reimagined, but this should be a run-heavy team again. Devin Roche had 5.7 yards per carry, not nearly as good as Trequan Jones’ 7.5 yards per pop, plus JUCO transfer Trey Hall was originally an Ole Miss commit. Quinn Henicle and Jaxon Potter will have skill guys to work with and Cook, who played at Kansas State and coached at Tennessee, was a logical guy to promote with Decker’s departure.

### Who gets more reps as the starting QB?

Henicle is the holdover and the guy who knows this system and scheme, but he also wasn’t very good last season. He ran for 4.8 yards per carry on 44 attempts and only completed 42.5% of his passes, as he was just 11-for-25 against a skeleton crew USF team in the bowl game. Meanwhile, Potter, who was a higher-graded recruit, was willing to come all the way from Washington State and head to the other coast as a California native. That said, Henicle was recruited to some FCS schools with good rushing attacks and also Army, so he was clearly viewed as an impact QB in the ground game. Neither guy looks poised to top Joseph’s numbers, but Rahne needs to get this right and fix it early in the season, if he doesn’t coming out of camp.

### Should we buy or sell this defense?

Rahne, an offensive-minded guy, seems to have finally rounded that side of the ball into form, going up in yards per carry and points per game in each of the last three seasons. However, the biggest separator for the Monarchs last season was Blake Seiler’s defense. That group shaved off 9.5 PPG and 0.9 YPP from the previous season, holding opponents to just 18.5 PPG and 4.8 YPP. As a team, ODU outgained opponents by 1.9 yards per play. Seiler saw the sack total go from 19 to 26 to 39 in a three-year span and put forth a top-25 third-down defense. Seiler also sees the return of two linebackers who started in 2024, but missed most of last season, and has returning starters at each level of the defense. I’ll buy that they’re better than 2024, but worse than 2025.
